By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlinear moment as an equivalence class of functions rather than a function. The polynomial of degree $N$ or formal power series ansatz of the invariance equation are the distinguished representatives of the equivalence class. We also show that, when the system is exponentially stable, the moment describes the output shared by all trajectories up to the order $k^-$, which gives the moment a time-domain interpretation when the steady-state interpretation is not available. Finally, we show that the concept of moment matching also naturally extends as the definition of nonlinear moment is extended to an equivalence class. The ansatz also plays a crucial role in the extended notion of moment matching. The results are illustrated by a numerical example.

title: SoK: Splitting the Trigger or Adding Attackers? Disentangling Distributed Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning
comment: 28 pages, 10 figures, 22 tables. Systematization of knowledge with original controlled experiments (875 paired federated learning runs). Under submission. Code and data: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/fl-pieces-artifact-BFF3/
summary: Distributed backdoor attacks split a trigger among several federated learning clients, so that the backdoor appears only in the aggregated model. Since DBA, a line of work has reported that such attacks are stronger, more persistent, and stealthier than a single attacker with the full trigger. We systematize this literature and test this belief. We code nineteen primary studies and fifteen papers that evaluate against DBA. The reported advantage is rarely measured against a complete trigger delivered by the same attackers, and none of the fifteen evaluations tests whether individual pieces remain effective. We then run 875 paired federated runs that separate adding attackers from splitting the trigger. In our image experiments, adding attackers raised attack success in every seed of all 30 cells where we measured it, by 7.5 to 83.4 percentage points on average. Splitting the trigger among the same attackers had a smaller effect, and its sign depended on the piece layout, the allocation, and the attackers' local training. With DBA's compact layout, splitting lowered attack success on CIFAR-10. A larger penalty on small CNNs vanished once the attackers trained longer, and an FCBA-style allocation gained a few points. Widely separated pieces helped on CIFAR-10, its grayscale version, and GTSRB. No model required all pieces. Neural Cleanse suppressed single pieces together with the full trigger, but split backdoors with separated pieces survived it better than complete ones. We derive reporting requirements for attack and defense evaluations.

title: Failure Modes and Data-Efficient Remedies for Transformer-Based Prediction of Viscoplastic Flows
summary: Fast and accurate prediction of viscoplastic flows remains a challenge in computational rheology due to yield surfaces, discontinuous gradients, and strongly nonlinear transitions between yielded and unyielded regions. Transformer-based neural operators such as RheOFormer have recently shown strong potential for surrogate modeling of non-Newtonian flows. However, their applicability to viscoplastic systems and their efficacy in recovering realistic flows remain poorly understood. In this work, we present the first systematic investigation of RheOFormer applied to steady Bingham channel flow. By isolating the problem to a simple geometry and constitutive model, we examine how dataset structure, numerical value range, and input representation govern the model's ability to interpolate and extrapolate within the parameter space. The data regimes in which RheOFormer remains accurate and those in which errors emerge are identified, particularly for plug-dominated flows and for conditions outside the velocity scales or flow structures represented during training. Upon identifying these failure modes, targeted enhancements to the input representation and loss formulation are introduced to better predict low-gradient plug regions. Logarithmic velocity representations and gradient-aware loss formulations substantially improve accuracy in challenging regimes where the baseline formulation fails. In addition, extrapolation errors are reduced by augmenting the training set with only a few strategically selected cases spanning the missing physical regimes. Finally, a single partially developed snapshot suffices for an accurate steady-state prediction, and the model outperforms simply copying its input throughout flow development. These results highlight the importance of appropriate field representation and parameter-space coverage for data-efficient neural-operator prediction of viscoplastic flows.

title: Stress2Twin: Profile-Driven Network Digital Twins for Guarded Edge Computing Resource Management
summary: Heterogeneous edge systems require resource managers to determine how many application replicas to deploy, where to place them, and how to distribute incoming requests while satisfying service-level performance constraints. Acquiring the performance knowledge required for these decisions through exhaustive multi-node characterization is measurement-intensive and becomes increasingly difficult as the number of workers and configurations grows. Stress2Twin is a profile-driven Network Digital Twin (NDT) framework that profiles edge nodes independently and composes their measured behavior into a system-level resource-management model. Machine-level oracles characterize latency, throughput, loss, queueing, and power as functions of assigned request rate and replica count. A guarded optimizer derives operating regions and tests neighboring request-rate states before retaining a replica count, reserving capacity before measured nonlinear degradation. Independent profiling of our three-worker Kubernetes testbed requires 271 measured states, corresponding to approximately 4.5 hours, compared with an estimated 123 hours for exhaustive characterization of the considered cluster configuration space. In a single-run ramp evaluation, the selected policy records no latency or loss-threshold violations within the derived 1,650 requests per second (RPS) supported range and reduces estimated power by 27.84% relative to RPS100 Round Robin (RR) placement. An additional single-run evaluation under a non-monotonic workload records no latency violation and 19.67% lower estimated energy than a stabilized RPS50 RR policy. These results show that independently acquired machine profiles can support capacity-aware resource consolidation within a measured operating range. Power savings use an idealized active-worker accounting model.

title: Rateless Lattices: Constructions, Coding Theorems, and Capacity
summary: A rateless code sends a fixed message as an unbounded stream of symbols such that every prefix is a codeword. We introduce rateless lattices, sequences of integral lattices of increasing dimension in which each lattice projects onto the first coordinates of the next while the induced finite codebooks retain constant size. Our first contribution is a family obtained from Construction D' with two nested Raptor codes. We derive generator matrices, volume, and an encoder. For every noise or fading sequence unknown to the transmitter and independent of the code randomness, we prove an ensemble random-coding bound for multistage decoding. These results quantify the loss created by a fixed split of information between two levels, and the bound remains valid for sparse LT stages of logarithmic degree. They concern recovery of the message, or finite-codeword residue; lattice-point recovery with a fixed alphabet incurs an additional coarse-lattice error term. We then show that the split loss is caused by stage-by-stage decoding. For a dense ensemble with ring coefficients, we characterize the rateless capacity region under joint decoding. With equal level sizes, the ensemble achieves the accumulated capacity of uniform pulse-amplitude modulation for two levels and for additional levels. Single-level $p$-ary rateless lattices achieve the same performance, satisfy a finite-parameter rateless Poltyrev inequality, and, with geometric shaping, approach within any $ε>0$ of the Gaussian incremental-redundancy capacity for bounded SNR. Repetition of a fixed-dimension lattice codeword instead incurs a loss that grows unboundedly with retransmissions. We also analyze a joint belief-propagation decoder over $\mathbb Z_4$ using density evolution on a tree-like surrogate ensemble. Simulations on AWGN and block-fading channels show that joint decoding removes most of the multistage-decoding loss.

title: Multi-Sensor Fusion for False-Alarm Reduction by Timed Electromechanical Corroboration
comment: 8 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
summary: A physician checks the clinical electrocardiogram against other observations. A wearable monitor has no physician. This paper shows that a mechanical sensor worn beside the electrocardiogram can take over that check, and that the right added sensors lower false alarms further. A beat is accepted only when a mechanical contraction follows at the delay learned for the wearer. Beat-shaped artifacts injected into resting and exercise recordings passed the electrocardiogram alone almost every time. A seismocardiogram or phonocardiogram as the second channel rejected most while keeping nearly all true beats, strongly at rest and partly during exercise. Shifting the mechanical signal in time removed the benefit. A detection criterion scores an added sensor by the part of its response that the sensors in place cannot predict. With four sensors, this score ranked the sets as their measured false-alarm rates did. With the two sensors it selected, 6.2 percent of the artifacts passed while 95 percent of true beats were kept, half the rate of the best single sensor. In integer arithmetic on a low-cost microcontroller, the detector made the same decisions as the software. These rates come from injected artifacts, not alarms in patients. Natural motion and clinical events remain untested.

title: Extended Deterministic Learning under Local Finite-Time Excitation
summary: This paper develops an extension of classical deterministic learning (CDL) for the regulation of uncertain nonlinear systems, referred to as Extended Deterministic Learning (EDL). CDL relies on periodic or recurrent closed-loop trajectories to ensure that the locally active radial-basis-function (RBF) neurons satisfy a partial persistence-of-excitation (PE) condition. During regulation, however, the state approaches a constant operating point and continued excitation disappears. EDL preserves the local-learning mechanism of CDL while enabling locally accurate learning under a local finite-time excitation (local FTE) condition, which requires neither persistent excitation nor recurrent system trajectories. Specifically, an adaptive RBF controller is combined with filtered finite-time data storage. Under local FTE, the resulting scheme guarantees that all closed-loop signals are uniformly ultimately bounded, the regulation state converges exponentially to a small neighborhood of the desired operating point, and the neural weights associated with the locally active RBFs converge exponentially to small neighborhoods of their ideal values. Consequently, the unknown nonlinear dynamics are learned locally and accurately over the experienced region without requiring persistent excitation after the finite learning interval. A numerical example illustrates the improvement in local learning achieved by EDL over CDL.

title: Weight-Space Backdoors in Open-Weight LLMs: Cross-Architecture Attacks and Blind Model Forensics
summary:
Open-weight language models are vulnerable to trigger-conditioned behaviors introduced through sparse post-training weight modifications, creating supply-chain risks beyond conventional provenance checks. We present Neural Sentinel, a cross-architecture study of gradient-guided backdoor insertion and model forensics spanning 18 checkpoints across 14 architecture families (124M-31.3B parameters), including state-space and recurrent models.
  On Phi-2, modifying approximately 0.0002% of parameters induced an exact short-marker output after 300 steps (332 seconds), with mean next-token KL divergence of $1.5 \times 10^{-5}$ and 100% top-1 agreement over evaluated positions of eight fixed reference prompts. Separate experiments produced structured tool-call-formatted outputs without establishing downstream execution. We identify three procedure-dependent response regimes -- Gradient-Permeable, Scale-Threshold, and Gradient-Fragmented -- and evaluate PPO-based weight-space exploration, which showed no statistically significant advantage over random search.
  For defense, Neural Sentinel combines weight-difference analysis, trigger discovery, activation probing, and contextual output inspection. In a 22-artifact development cohort, its reference-optional scanner classified 4/5 backdoored artifacts as BACKDOORED; the remaining positive and all 17 clean artifacts were SUSPICIOUS. These findings establish the feasibility of sparse conditional-output insertion and evidence-producing forensic triage, while identifying limitations in behavioral-drift assessment and clean-model admission.

title: SONATI: Spatio-temporal ocean neighbourhood asymmetric transformer for imputation of sparse, tabular data with uncertainty
summary: Missing value imputation is often a prerequisite for downstream analyses. In oceanography, observational data are frequently structured in a tabular manner, highly sparse and exhibit spatio-temporal structures that classical imputers such as k-nearest neighbours or MissForest are not suited to exploit. We present the Spatio-temporal Ocean Neighbourhood Asymmetric Transformer for Imputation (SONATI), a masked, factorised time-space transformer operating on pre-computed, local time and space neighbourhoods, which reduces computational complexity compared to global attention. SONATI is designed to work with tabular data and is thus in principle able to work on both gridded and unstructured data, though evaluation here was performed on gridded North Atlantic data only. It provides aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties through a negative log-likelihood loss and multiple forward passes with Monte Carlo dropout. Systematic ablations on attention type and masking strategies guided the final architecture design. The results showed that SONATI outperformed classical and transformer-based methods by at least 12.5% in terms of root mean squared error (RMSE) on a large observational oceanographic dataset with key biogeochemical and physical parameters in the North Atlantic (potential temperature, salinity, oxygen, nitrate, silicate and phosphate). Attention type and masking strategy strongly affected imputation accuracy and smoothness of the produced oceanographic fields. Best results were achieved by factorised time-space attention and combined geographic and per-sample masking. The combined masking strategy reduced the imputation error by 14.3% compared to per-sample masking only. Uncertainties were moderately well calibrated (miscalibration area at observed locations $0.074\pm0.012$) and moderately correlated with the imputation error.

title: Connected but Late: Sample Age of Commercial BLE Wearables under Wi-Fi Coexistence for Real-Time Clinical Applications
summary: Wearable sensors are increasingly being used in real-time clinical applications, such as rehabilitation robots and live therapy monitoring. As Healthcare 5.0 moves towards personalized therapies, their use will continue growing, potentially compromising communication reliability. Most wearables transmit over Bluetooth Low Energy, sharing 2.4 GHz with institutional Wi-Fi. Previous coexistence studies have focused on whether data arrive, rather than when. We measured sample age for a commercial electrocardiogram strap, from acquisition through the gateway to storage in our platform MEDWEAR, in an anechoic chamber and a hospital rehabilitation gym, and we compared it with illustrative clinical deadlines. Without load, the strap's own framing was the largest source of delay, making samples on average 280 ms and up to 550 ms old before transmission. Wi-Fi load had no measurable effect while adaptive frequency hopping could avoid the loaded channel. In a stress test, which forced the link onto the loaded channel, the link became the dominant source of delay, adding up to 11 s. The link stayed connected, but a median of 29% of samples and up to 98% (worst case) were older than 1 s on arrival at the gateway. The gym behaved mostly like the quiet chamber, but during one traffic burst, while hopping was restricted, up to 4.6% of samples were older than 1 s. These results show that a connected link can deliver late data. Therefore, sensors intended for real-time clinical applications should be profiled in situ and monitored based on sample age rather than connection status alone.

title: Cramer-Rao Bound Minimization for Discrete SIM-aided ISAC Systems
summary: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM) have recently emerged as a promising wave-domain signal processing architecture for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), owing to the capability of efficient beamforming with reduced number of radio-frequency chains. However, most existing SIM-aided ISAC designs rely on maximizing beampattern gain under continuous phase shifts, which cannot explicitly characterize the fundamental estimation accuracy under practical deployment. In this paper, we investigate Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) minimization problem for a discrete SIM-aided ISAC system. To tackle the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a two-stage transmit design that decouples CRB optimization from cascaded multi-layer SIM realization. In the first stage, an ideal precoder is obtained. In the second stage, it is synthesized on the practical SIM by alternating power allocation and phase-shift updates, with a closed-form discrete projection and linearized QoS constraints. Numerical results demonstrate fast convergence, reveal the sensing-communication trade-off, and verify CRB improvements with higher phase resolution and larger SIM configurations.

title: TrustFlow-ECG: Reliability-Aware ECG Restoration with Calibrated Risk Estimation
summary: Electrocardiogram (ECG) restoration models can reduce noise and motion artifacts, but they rarely estimate whether the restored waveform is reliable for downstream analysis. We propose TrustFlow-ECG, a reliability-aware restoration framework that combines a one-step conditional rectified-flow restorer with a lightweight window-level risk predictor. The predictor uses the noisy ECG, restored ECG, and correction residual, then applies validation-set isotonic calibration for selective ECG analysis. We evaluate on MIT-BIH ECG windows corrupted with NSTDB artifacts, powerline interference, and mixed noise across multiple SNRs, with an external 9,675-window PTB-XL stress check without retraining. TrustFlow achieves 0.862 Spearman correlation with true risk and 0.911 AUROC for failure detection, while calibration reduces ECE from 0.0385 to 0.0098. At 80% coverage, selective rejection reduces RMSE from 0.1848 to 0.1345, improves R-peak F1 from 0.8778 to 0.9175, and reduces HR MAE from 6.26 to 4.88 bpm.

title: Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels---Part I: Stabilization in Polar Coordinates
summary: A surface vessel with surge force and yaw moment as inputs and no sway actuation cannot be stabilized at a fixed pose by continuous time-invariant feedback. We introduce a zero-sideslip point, a point whose position relative to the hull depends on the surge and sway speeds and whose velocity points along the vessel's heading at every instant, and show that it moves as a unicycle. This reduction allows the time-invariant, polar-coordinate steering laws of Todorovski et al. (2025) to be applied to the underactuated vessel without modification. With two steering laws, GloBa and BoLSA, we construct strict control Lyapunov functions and prove global asymptotic stability, first for a four-state model with surge speed and yaw rate as virtual inputs, and then, by one step of backstepping, for the full six-state model with surge force and yaw moment. The analysis extends to hulls with fore-aft asymmetric sway-yaw damping, excluded in prior work by the assumption of diagonal damping. Unlike prior time-varying designs, the time-invariant controller yields smooth, non-oscillatory trajectories, an important practical advantage for docking. The designs are validated in simulation on the Cybership I hull model.

title: Praxis: Practical Witness Encryption for NP
summary:
Witness encryption encrypts a message to an NP statement so that whoever holds a witness can decrypt. Over a decade after its introduction, known constructions for general NP statements are far from practical or rest on heuristic or broken assumptions. We propose Praxis, a practical scheme for NP, and prove it extractable in the bilinear generic group and random oracle models under Module-SIS. Our instantiation encrypts to a Groth16 verifier on BN254, set up honestly, which serves every NP relation at the same cost: at $100$-bit security, its ciphertext is $7.88$ GiB, encryption takes $2^{34.2}$ base-field multiplications, and decryption with a Groth16 proof $2^{33.0}$ on average. We give Lean 4 proofs of correctness and extraction at this instantiation's parameters.
  Praxis starts from the rank-gap template of the recent feasibility result [Hair and Sahai, arXiv 2026]. Where they raise the gap to keep decryption polynomial, we fix it, so decryption ends with a search that is exponential but concretely fast: $O(2^{λ/4} N^{1/4})$ expected operations for a statement in $N$ Boolean unknowns at $λ$-bit security. A quadratic arithmetic program makes our hidden matrix low rank, so where their ciphertext encodes a basis of a matrix space, ours holds factors of width two, which a pairing multiplies. Weights and identities from an extension field tie copies of this matrix, so an adversary telling encryptions apart yields a witness or a Module-SIS solution. For the same Groth16 statement and $100$-bit security level, Praxis reduces the ciphertext size and the cost of encryption of either of their constructions by over ten orders of magnitude, and that of decryption by over six.

title: What Do Differentiable Rule Learners Need? FLARE: Fuzzy Rules with Additive Evidence
summary: Rule learners are used where transparency and accountability are required, because they give practitioners patterns they can read. Learning rules is a discrete problem, so neurosymbolic pipelines that use rules as explanations rely on relaxations such as the straight-through estimator. However, these differentiable rule learners often lag behind both classical rule learners and black-box classifiers in terms of performance. We study which parts of a rule-based classifier affect performance, and how well gradient-based training learns each of them. We found that most of the performance comes from how the rules are weighted: random rules with learned weights are already more accurate than every published differentiable rule learner we tested. Based on our results, we propose FLARE (Fuzzy Learned-Antecedent Rule Evidence), a differentiable rule learner that learns simple rules that combine to make the final decision. We also propose a learned encoding for variables with thousands of categories. We test FLARE on tabular data, using 42 datasets of OpenML-CC18 and the 38 classification tasks of TabArena. On CC18, FLARE exceeds the compared rule learners by 7.69 to 12.38 macro-F1 points and performs comparably to random forests, while remaining 1.00 to 1.11 points below tuned gradient-boosted trees. On TabArena it ranks at the same level as random forests and ahead of the other rule learners. As the concept-to-label head of a concept bottleneck model, FLARE is the best rule-based head in five of six settings. On graphs, it is competitive on PubMed and EMOGI but falls behind graph neural networks on Cora and Citeseer. Our code is available at https://github.com/Fuminides/FLARE

title: Geometry, Reliability, and Spacetime Dynamics of Hyper-Simplex Fractal Networks
comment: 49 pages (19 pp. main text & refs, Appendices A-F from p. 20), 23 numbered figures (24 graphic files), 13 numbered tables. Unified formal theory of the sparse node-anchored hyper-simplex fractal network G(N,m), superseding arXiv:2410.00583v1. Lean 4 mechanization: https://github.com/Tongji708A/hsfn-lean (49 modules, 853 kernel-audited statements, zero sorry, commit 664b9d7)
summary: Large-scale, delay-tolerant peer-to-peer networks that need strong consistency usually separate naming, routing, consensus, and ordering into independent layers. To bring deterministic network properties into complex peer-to-peer structures, we unify all four on a single recursive topology. Modeling mutual equality among N peers in Euclidean space requires dimension at least N-1, which prevents flat equal groups from scaling at fixed dimension. The hyper-simplex fractal network G(N,m) escapes this limit by recursion. Each non-leaf node anchors a half-scale N-clique. From the resulting digit-word addresses alone, nodes decide adjacency without routing tables, forward greedily along exact shortest paths, and converge geometrically to a self-similar attractor of dimension log_2 N. Running hierarchical PBFT on the same prefix tree achieves linear message load and logarithmic fault-free latency, with an explicit reliability threshold under independent faults and analytical recursions for anchor exposure, dual homing, and event registration. Reversible topology edits generate the Higman-Thompson group V_N on the address boundary, block order characterizes service-topology hosting beyond treewidth, and root-anchored block heights yield persistent spacetime coordinates with compact light-client proofs.

title: Rateless Lattice Codes over Fading Wiretap Channels: Finite-Length Secrecy and the Secret-Key Capacity of Degraded Sessions
summary: In rateless transmission the transmitter keeps sending until the legitimate receiver (Bob) can decode. Over a wiretap channel this has a useful side effect: the eavesdropper (Eve) sees only as many symbols as Bob needs, although the transmitter knows neither channel. We study the secrecy of rateless lattice codes in this setting. First, using a public dither and privacy amplification, we prove a finite-length secrecy bound, in total variation distance, for every channel realization, even if Eve knows all codes and seeds and combines all packets. Second, stopping when Bob acknowledges successful decoding, as in hybrid ARQ, costs at most the logarithm of the number of possible feedback outcomes in secret bits. Third, for degraded sessions with state-based stopping and without a pre-shared key or other public discussion, the secret-key rate of a session cannot exceed its accumulated Gaussian secrecy capacity, and adaptive key generation with shaped rateless lattice codes comes within any $ε>0$ of this limit when Eve's channel states are revealed after the session. If only their statistics are known, choosing the key length after the session guarantees a prescribed secrecy-outage probability. Finally, over block Rayleigh fading with a CRC-based acknowledgement and joint belief-propagation decoding, and with Eve $20$~dB weaker on average, the scheme reaches $59$--$69\%$ of the outage-weighted throughput of an ideal infinite-length secure hybrid-ARQ benchmark for Bob SNRs of $8$--$20$~dB.

title: Near-Field Physical-Layer Authentication Under Noisy Enrollment
summary: In near-field physical-layer authentication (PLA), the receiver estimates a spatial reference from noisy enrollment pilots. With a fixed residual-energy threshold, even a small reference error can cause the false rejection (FR) probability to approach one as the received energy increases. We derive the distribution of the overlap between the true and enrolled spatial directions and use it to calibrate a test based on the aligned energy and the residual-to-aligned energy ratio. The calibration bounds FR for arbitrary regional gains and all legitimate received energies above a prescribed minimum. For a fixed enrolled reference, we reduce the problem of finding the maximum acceptance probability of a multi-antenna attacker to a one-dimensional search. We also derive a pre-enrollment upper bound that holds when the attacker chooses its precoder after observing the enrolled reference. For a single region and a fixed angular threshold, the enrollment energy sufficient to preserve angular separation grows inversely with the square of the available angular margin. In the numerical study with 128 receive elements at 28 GHz, the FR upper bound was 0.9984, including the enrollment outage allowance. At a regional phase perturbation of 20, four regions provided the best trade-off among the tested partitions: its simulated FR was 0.1442, while its false acceptance (FA) at 9 m was 1.084 under the fixed transmit-energy setting.

title: Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels---Part II: Underway Docking
summary: In underway directional docking, a second-order nonholonomic problem, six pairs of states of two vehicles have to be made to match by two inputs. The key challenge is to design time-invariant feedback of the relative states and the leader's measured motion only, which makes the follower's convergence in range outpaced, with no sway actuation whatsoever, by the bearing and heading convergence of the follower relative to the leader's path. We begin with nonmodular backstepping, choosing speed and commanded heading jointly to control range and bearing. Curvature compensation and normalization of angular errors by different powers of range remove the range singularity from the model. Our construction passes from unicycle kinematics to the ships' zero-sideslip points and through the sway dynamics to the physical hulls. The design extends to a leader with a different hull and to a docking point astern or abeam of the leader, where we show that, while the leader turns, a follower without sway actuation holds the point only with a heading that differs from the leader's. With strict control Lyapunov construction, we achieve global $κ$-exponential convergence, with a rate independent of the initial error.

title: A Model Obfuscation and Controllable Authorization Scheme for Deep Learning as a Service
summary: Developing deep learning models requires substantial computational and data resources, making them core intellectual assets for enterprises. As Deep Learning as a Service (DLaaS) increasingly extends to edge computing environments, models deployed on third-party devices face growing threats from reverse engineering. Existing model protection methods often depend on specialized hardware or incur substantial computational overhead, while lacking effective mechanisms for controlling model usage. There is therefore a need for lightweight solutions that combine model protection with controllable authorization. To address this challenge, we propose KeyObf, a model obfuscation and controllable authorization scheme for DLaaS. KeyObf efficiently protects model parameters and architecture through model obfuscation while binding parameter recovery to user keys, ensuring that only authorized users can perform inference correctly. By integrating a key-based mechanism into the obfuscation framework, KeyObf unifies model protection and controllable authorization. Experimental results demonstrate that KeyObf preserves the inference accuracy of authorized users, rejects inference requests when credential authentication fails, and increases the difficulty of recovering model information under the evaluated reverse-engineering conditions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a lightweight approach to model protection and controllable authorization in third-party deployment scenarios.

title: Scalable Beckmann Maps Improve One-step Generation
comment: 40 pages, 15 figures, 12 tables. Code and checkpoints: https://tullebulle.github.io/projects/sbm/
summary: Beckmann Transport Models (BTM) learn one-step generative maps end-to-end from data, without a teacher, a distillation stage, or pretrained features. We introduce Scalable Beckmann Maps (SBM), which bring to BTM the two ingredients behind the quality of modern multistep generators: classifier-free guidance (CFG) and a training recipe that scales, while keeping sampling at a single network evaluation. CFG combines conditional and unconditional velocity or score predictions, which a Beckmann map does not have. Our guidance rests on one observation: the BTM current is a positive multiple of an autonomous denoising field, to which CFG applies as it does to a velocity. With exact denoisers this gives guided BTM. In practice we substitute the map's own conditional and null predictions for the denoisers, which requires no additional network and introduces a bias that we characterize. We show that the guided update is consistent with a guided conservation equation, and that guidance can move the boundaries between basins, sending more noise to the modes a condition favors. Trained from scratch in the latent of a representation autoencoder, SBM reaches a one-step FID of 1.6 on ImageNet 256x256 without a teacher or a feature loss, outperforming the Improved-MeanFlow baseline with 3.2x fewer FLOPs. In text-to-image generation it reaches a GenEval score of 0.86 with one network evaluation. As a world model, where we train without guidance, the recipe alone outperforms DriftWorld on all five metrics of two robot-manipulation benchmarks, with 1.9-2.8x less training compute and no pretrained auxiliary feature encoder.

title: Schism: Reconfigurable Scale-Up Domains for Distributed Quantum Computing
summary:
Switch-based quantum datacenters connect quantum processing units (QPUs) through photonic switches and shared Bell-state measurement (BSM) devices. Sharing BSMs saves hardware, but fixed connectivity constrains access to these resources. Local communication can overload one rack's BSMs while others remain idle; reaching those idle resources incurs additional optical loss and retries through switches and quantum frequency converters (QFCs). Programs remain locked into this locality-contention tradeoff as their communication patterns change.
  We propose Schism, an architecture that lets programs dynamically change which QPUs share each BSM pool. Schism places BSM pools at aggregation switches and QFCs on their core-facing uplinks. Top-of-rack switches establish reconfigurable native-wavelength circuits from QPUs to these pools, forming scale-up domains bounded by the optical loss budget. Reconfiguration reshapes resource sharing across racks without moving QPUs or migrating quantum states. Our key insight is that QPU grouping jointly determines photon-path loss and contention for BSM resources: locality alone cannot identify the best grouping, and a grouping pays off only if its savings outweigh the delay of reconfiguring to it. We develop an optimization framework that combines graph partitioning with resource-constrained completion-time estimates and dynamic programming to select how QPUs share BSM pools and when those groupings reconfigure, between or within circuit phases.
  Our evaluation using SeQUeNCe with trapped-ion parameters shows that Schism achieves communication speedups of 4.9-7.3x across 11 workloads on 32 QPUs compared to Fixed Clos connectivity and 3.6-8.3x compared to SwitchQNet. Schism also outperforms a hypothetical network-wide switch by 1.35-1.38x on the eight workloads whose phases fit in a pool, and trails it by 1.1-1.75x on the other three.

title: Extensive-Rank Matrix Denoising Under i.i.d. Non-Gaussian Noise
summary: We study extensive-rank matrix denoising for rotationally invariant signals corrupted by i.i.d. non-Gaussian noise. To exploit both the signal spectrum and the entrywise noise prior, we consider an orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP) algorithm that alternates between a rotationally invariant spectral estimator and an entrywise denoiser. At each OAMP iteration, we conjecture a high-dimensional Gaussian equivalence property: the entrywise module admits an effective additive scalar Gaussian channel, whereas the spectral module behaves as if corrupted by i.i.d. Gaussian noise of matching variance. Under this conjecture, we formulate a state evolution (SE) recursion for the effective noise variances of both modules. Numerical simulations confirm that the SE predictions closely track the empirical mean-square errors. For robust principal component analysis (PCA), we apply this OAMP algorithm and characterize its recovery phase diagram via SE. Numerical results show that OAMP achieves a larger recovery region than several existing methods.

title: WAFT: A Fourier-Analytic Framework for Steady-State Performance of Walker Constellations
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
summary: The Walker configuration is predominantly adopted by nongeostationary orbit constellations exemplified by Starlink and Kuiper. The steady-state distribution of aggregate downlink interference power is critical for spectrum coexistence regulation. Large-scale time-stepped simulation and stochastic geometry (SG)-based models are the mainstream methods for obtaining the distribution, but are either computationally expensive or subject to inherent bias. This paper models the aggregate downlink interference power as an additive observable and proposes the Walker-constellation Analysis via Fourier Transform (WAFT) framework to derive the steady-state performance. Modeling the constellation as a periodic impulse array on the phase torus, the spectral representation of the observable is derived via 2-D Fourier analysis. Analytical expressions for the expectation, variance, and steady-state complementary cumulative distribution function are further derived, and the periodicity of receiver performance along longitude is characterized. For a Starlink sub-constellation example, numerical validation shows that the percentile discrepancies of WAFT relative to a finite-duration time-stepped simulation remain within 0.09~dB. Comparisons with isotropic and intensity-matched SG models reveal that the conditional independence of satellite positions alone makes the models assign a substantial probability mass to physically infeasible values, producing percentile discrepancies.

title: PAC Infinite-Time Safety Guarantees for Stochastic Systems with Unknown Probabilistic Distributions
summary: This paper studies infinite-time safety certification for discrete-time stochastic systems with continuous dynamics and unknown disturbance distributions that have full support on a known compact disturbance set. We develop a probably approximately correct (PAC) data-driven framework that uses only finitely many i.i.d. disturbance samples: with confidence at least $1-δ$, if the certification procedure accepts a candidate certificate defining a nonempty subset of a prescribed compact safe set, then the system, starting from any state in this subset, remains within the safe set for all future times with probability at least $1-ε$. Our approach builds on a fundamental characterization of infinite-time safety. We first prove that a robust invariant set exists within a compact safe set if and only if there exists an initial state from which the system remains in the safe set indefinitely with positive probability. This reduces infinite-time safety certification to two tractable subproblems: robust invariant-set computation and finite-horizon reach-avoid certification. We first compute a robust invariant set within the safe set, then use i.i.d. disturbance samples to certify, with PAC guarantees, a subset of initial states for which the probability of reaching this set within a finite horizon while remaining safe is at least a prescribed threshold. To our knowledge, this is the first PAC framework for infinite-time safety under unknown disturbance distributions. Finally, illustrative examples demonstrate the method using semi-definite programming.

title: Anti OS Fingerprinting, Revisited: A Loadable Kernel Module for FreeBSD and What Twenty-Five Years Changed
comment: 8 pages, 7 tables. Code and measurement scripts: https://github.com/daisu-mi/aod
summary: In 2001 we published a paper on an Anti OS Detection (AoD) system: a modified FreeBSD 4.3 kernel that makes a host answer the probes of an OS fingerprinting tool as if it ran another operating system. This report revisits that work on FreeBSD 15.1. We do not claim a new method. We report three things. First, the same goal is now reachable from a loadable module of about 800 lines that uses the packet filter hook interface and sets one kernel variable, without changing the kernel source. Second, the module covers both active and passive fingerprinting: Nmap 7.98 reports an exact match for Linux and for Windows 10/11, and p0f 3 reports the same systems from the connections the host opens. Third, an exact match in Nmap was not enough: a passive tool, plain FIN scans and a comparison with real hosts each exposed a mismatch that the previous step could not see. A real Windows 11 host and the final Windows personality get the same verdict from Nmap and the same signatures from p0f and JA4T; a real Linux 7.0 host is not an exact match in Nmap at all, while the personality built from Nmap's database is. We describe those mismatches, how we removed them, what the module costs, and what it still cannot hide.

title: Benchmarking EEG feature families for ADHD research in children and adolescents: performance and explainability across attention tasks
comment: 20 pages, 3 figures. Benchmark software and aggregate results (v1.0.0): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23884319. Curated EEG dataset (v1.0.0): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21982978
summary: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder varies in presentation. Diagnosis requires clinical and developmental assessment. Reproducible electroencephalography measures may complement clinical and behavioural characterisation, but differing feature definitions and evaluation methods hinder comparison. We compared seven feature families and four combinations across attention tasks and assessed the stability of held-out explanations. Two serious games yielded four overlapping attention-task cohorts of 123-140 participants each. Repeated nested participant-held-out evaluation assessed recruitment-group discrimination. Exploratory paired participant-cluster bootstrap tests corrected for multiplicity in two separate families: 72 individual-task contrasts and 18 fusion contrasts. For eight configurations selected after inspecting predictive results, we explained held-out native probabilities before calibration. In the strongest task context, the highest configuration mean AUROC over three repetitions was 0.773, with a fixed-prediction 95% interval of 0.692-0.854 unadjusted for selecting the maximum. Precision, sensitivity and specificity were 0.740, 0.556 and 0.861. In that task, the paired AUROC difference for connectivity minus spectral features averaged +0.2083 across six classifiers and the common 8 s and 16 s durations, with pointwise 95% CI 0.1076-0.3072 and adjusted p = 0.0036. F4-AF4 beta-band coherence led repetition-level attribution summaries in five selected procedures and was selected in every fit. Other contexts showed weaker discrimination and less consistent retention of leading scientific inputs. No general classifier winner emerged. Connectivity and its recurring coherence input warrant independent replication, but do not justify a universal feature recommendation. These exploratory findings do not establish causal task effects, disease mechanisms or diagnostic validity.

title: Mitigating Nested GTP Attacks: A Closed-Loop eBPF Defense for 5G and Beyond Networks
summary:
The evolving cellular networks continue to rely on the legacy GPRS Tunneling Protocol-User Plane (GTP-U) to encapsulate and route user data traffic across the data plane. Recent security research demonstrated that nested GTP-U (GTP-in-GTP) payload vulnerabilities enable a diverse range of attacks on victim users. To address this vulnerability, in this paper, we propose a closed-loop extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) and eXpress Data Path (XDP) defense to detect and mitigate nested GTP-U attacks in 5G and beyond networks. The proposed framework contains three components: an in-kernel XDP Detection and Drop Module (XDP-DDM), a user-space User-Plane Telemetry Agent (UP-TA), and a multi-threaded Control-Plane Mitigation Orchestrator (CP-MO).
  We implement and evaluate the proposed defense on a sliced 5G testbed integrating Free5GC, UERANSIM, and Containerlab. Experimental results indicate that the XDP-DDM detects and drops malicious nested GTP-U packets at line rate, while the UP-TA and CP-MO asynchronously report and revoke the attacker's network access, respectively. Under a 10,000 packets-per-second cross-slice nested GTP-U flood, the proposed solution preserves the baseline performance of the victim slices while introducing minimal overhead. We also show that the proposed solution has minimal impact on the user's throughput and round-trip time.

title: Almost-Isometric Embeddings of Graphs into Riemannian Manifolds
summary: Graphs represent objects as vertices and relationships as edges; positive edge weights define shortest-path metrics. Metric embeddings leverage target-space geometry to analyze distances. Foundational results target linear spaces: Nash embedded Riemannian manifolds isometrically into Euclidean space, and Bourgain embedded $n$-point metrics into Hilbert space with $O(\log n)$ distortion. By contrast, the manifold hypothesis places high-dimensional data near low-dimensional smooth manifolds, making such manifolds themselves target spaces. What distortion is needed to embed a finite graph metric into such a manifold with its intrinsic distance? Although the star $K_{1,3}$ cannot embed isometrically into any complete Riemannian manifold, we prove almost-isometric embeddings always exist: for $\varepsilon>0$ and any finite connected positively weighted graph, we construct a smooth connected closed orientable surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ admitting a noncontractive $(1+\varepsilon)$-embedding of its vertices, with $\varepsilon$ arbitrarily small and independent of graph parameters. This construction transfers communication schemes between graphs and surfaces. For independent unicasts, fractional routing splits flows across paths while network coding lets relays combine messages. Space information flow permits relays anywhere, charging bandwidth times distance. Whereas coding advantage (optimal routing over coding cost) equals one in Euclidean space, we prove coding advantages on finite positively weighted undirected graphs transfer to smooth closed surfaces within factors approaching one. Counterexamples to the multiple-unicast conjecture and amplification yield smooth closed surfaces with unbounded coding advantage. Conversely, coding advantage is at most $C\log(g+2)$ on finite undirected graphs of orientable genus $g$ and smooth closed orientable surfaces of genus $g$, for absolute $C$.

title: On linear MMSE receivers in the presence of data-like multiuser interference
summary: Linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receivers have been of great interest for many decades for multi-user interference (MUI) mitigation in radiocommunications networks in particular. Despite the extensive literature on this subject, this topic remains relevant to several current and emerging applications. In this context, the paper presents a continuous-time approach showing that most of LMME receivers of the literature are suboptimal. In particular, they are typically implemented at the symbol rate following matched filtering to the pulse-shaping filter and require a prior knowledge of the MUI channels, which can be difficult and costly to acquire in practice. The main contribution of this paper is to address the key challenge of designing new LMMSE receivers that achieve the performance of the optimal receiver without requiring prior knowledge of the MUI channels. To this end, two novel receiver LMMSE structures are proposed and analyzed for linearly modulated signals impaired by data-like MUI: a two-input receiver and a three-input receiver. The proposed receivers are shown to be quasi-optimal over a broad range of scenarios. These results provide new perspectives for practical implementation of the optimal LMMSE receiver in the presence of data-like MUI, relying only on knowledge of the signal-of-interest (SOI) channel.

title: Advanced Reactance Method - A Novel Approach for Distance Protection in Presence of Grid-Following Inverter-Based-Resources
summary:
Renewable Energy Sources and consequently inverter-based resources (IBRs) are increasing worldwide.
  Grid-following (GFL) IBR control is the state-of-the-art.
  GFL IBRs exhibit different fault behavior compared to classical synchronous generators -- particularly in terms of Fault-Ride-Through (FRT) characteristics, which are critical for grid protection relaying.
  Grid protection must work securely, selectively and dependably, regardless of the feeding source.
  As common protection algorithms are designed for fault behavior determined by synchronous generators, their performance is expected to be compromised in the presence of GFL IBRs.
  Distance Protection is a widely used protection algorithm at all voltage levels.
  Literature shows that the FRT behavior of GFL IBRs impacts the Distance Protection relaying adversely.
  This paper proposes the Advanced Reactance Method, a further development of the Classical Reactance Method for Distance Protection in the presence of GFL IBRs.
  The key idea of the proposed method is to make the algorithm independent of the feeding source impedance.
  Therefore, the negative sequence voltage is taken into account along with the negative sequence current.
  This makes the algorithm independent of the FRT behavior of GFL IBRs, even in case of suppression of negative sequence current during unsymmetrical faults.
  Moreover, correct settings for the classical method in the presence of GFL IBRs are presented as a solution for relays without the advanced method.
  The novel algorithm is evaluated against the correctly parameterized Classical Reactance Method and the Distance Protection algorithm.

title: InstantCoFFEA: Fast and accurate Tor flow correlation at realistic scale
summary: Tor end-to-end correlation attacks can link a client to its destination by matching traffic observed at both ends of a Tor circuit. However, their practical threat remains unclear for two reasons: existing correlation methods rely on O(N^2) pairwise processing, and prior works do not reflect the flow counts and base rates seen by realistic adversaries. We present InstantCoFFEA, which replaces exhaustive pairwise search with approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) retrieval using CAGRA and introduces ranked voting. At N = 200k, InstantCoFFEA is 14.56x faster than DeepCoFFEA and improves PR-AUC from 0.94 to 0.96. We also use TorPS to estimate the flow counts and matching-pair base rates observed by relay-level and network-level adversaries. Our simulations show that realistic attacks involve substantially more candidate flows and much lower base rates than those used in prior evaluations. Under a low-base-rate setting, PR-AUC drops for all methods, but InstantCoFFEA achieves 0.53 compared with 0.42 for DeepCoFFEA. These results show that evaluating correlation attacks requires considering both computational scale and the sparsity of true matching pairs.

title: AV-FLARE: Feature-Level Reliability Estimation for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
comment: Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 2027 IEEE Symposium Series on Computational Intelligence (IEEE SSCI 2027)
summary: Multimodal emotion recognition (MMER) systems typically rely on learned feature representations and attention mechanisms that implicitly weight information across time and modalities. However, these mechanisms do not explicitly incorporate input reliability, despite the presence of noise in audio, occlusions in visual data, and the sparse and event-driven nature of affective cues. We propose AV-FLARE, a framework that explicitly estimates fine-grained reliability scores across both temporal and feature dimensions prior to temporal modeling and uses them to modulate feature representations. Reliability is computed using two complementary components: (i) a supervised network trained jointly with the classification objective, and (ii) an unsupervised Gaussian Mixture Model that models global feature distributions. These signals are combined to provide both task-driven and distribution-aware reliability estimates. To integrate modalities, we introduce a hierarchical cross-modal attention mechanism in which textual features are used to guide audio-visual fusion as a semantic reference modality. Experiments on the IEMOCAP dataset show that AV-FLARE improves over a no-reliability baseline, achieving 90.81\% accuracy and 81.69\% F1-score, corresponding to gains of +4.41% and +8.56%, respectively. These results suggest that incorporating explicit input reliability estimation may improve robustness in multimodal emotion recognition under the evaluated setting.

title: Tightness of the Partition Bound for Multiterminal Secret Key Capacity
summary:
We consider secret key agreement among \(m\) terminals, each
  observing one component of a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless
  multiple source. The terminals communicate over a noiseless public
  channel, and a target set \(A\subseteq[m]\) seeks to generate a
  shared secret key, with the remaining terminals acting as helpers.
  The partition-based Csiszár--Narayan upper bound on secret key
  capacity is known to be tight without helpers but can be strict
  in their presence. We give a complete characterization of its tightness:
  for \(2\leq |A|\leq m\), the bound is tight for every source if and only if
  \(|A|\in\{2,m-2,m-1,m\}\). To prove tightness, we use the
  supermodularity of conditional entropy and the structure of
  optimal supports in the linear program for communication for
  omniscience. We first establish the result under strict
  supermodularity and then remove this assumption by a
  perturbation argument. For all remaining pairs \((m,|A|)\),
  we extend Chan's six-terminal counterexample. We also study
  optimal partitions when there are two target terminals and
  the source is a Markov random field on a connected graph.
  We show that an optimal bipartition separating the targets
  can be chosen so that both blocks induce connected subgraphs.
  For cycles, this reduces the number of candidate bipartitions
  from exponential to at most quadratic in \(m\).

title: A Closed-Form Soft Spectral Partition for Adaptive Mode Decomposition
comment: 27 pages, 9 figures. Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing. Code: https://github.com/plustar/A-Closed-Form-Soft-Spectral-Partition-for-Adaptive-Mode-Decomposition
summary: Density-based Adaptive Mode Decomposition (DAMD) shows that the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) objective, restricted to hard binary partitions, is equivalent to weighted K-means clustering, enabling automatic mode detection. The equivalence concerns detection only; extraction with hard Voronoi masks introduces boundary artefacts. This paper develops a soft extraction theory independent of the detector. First, the hard-partition equivalence is shown to be an algebraic identity that holds if and only if the weights are binary; hard and soft extraction are optima of two different functionals (linear K-means and regularised quadratic VMD) over the same simplex. Second, the regularised soft VMD problem is proved to have a closed-form global optimum, unique on the support of the spectrum: the Lorentzian-weighted partition $s_k^*(ω)\propto[1+2α(ω-ω_k)^2]^{-1}$. Every fixed point of the VMD ADMM mode update is proportional to $|ω-ω_k|^{-2}$; when the dual ascent enforces reconstruction, it is the $α\to\infty$ endpoint of this family. The Lorentzian shape at finite $α$ is therefore a consequence of the regulariser, and $α$ controls how closely the allocation approaches that fixed point. Third, under a Lorentzian spectral prior the partition equals the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimator of each mode in the low-noise limit, tying $α$ to the inverse squared mode bandwidth. Since the partition needs only detected centre frequencies, the extraction rule can be switched without recomputing detection. Synthetic experiments with known ground truth test the predictions; four categories of real signals show how much the two allocations differ.

title: Separating physics from discrepancy: Orthogonalized kernels for physics-encoded system identification
summary: Physics-encoded identification combines a physical model with a data-driven correction, but the data alone do not determine how the input-output map is split between them: components representable by the physical model may be assigned to either part. In kernel-based model embedding, this allocation is governed by the kernel. As a consequence, the physical parameters lack a well-defined target. In this work, this ambiguity is resolved a priori by defining a canonical physical parameter as the parameter of the physical model that best approximates the noise-free map, in a weighted least-squares sense, over a user-defined operating domain, together with an orthogonal discrepancy. Specifically, an orthogonalized kernel is derived that restricts the correction to functions orthogonal to the physical model. The resulting estimator keeps the closed-form solution of model embedding, while the canonical parameter depends only on the prescribed geometry, not on the kernel or the data. As the inputs become dense and the noise vanishes, the set of parameters consistent with the data converges to the canonical parameter, a property that generally fails without orthogonalization. Under energy-bounded noise, suitable regularization attains optimal worst-case estimation accuracy. Numerical examples demonstrate consistent parameter estimates across different kernels and experiments.

title: QUISA: A Compact, Flexible and Unified Instruction-Set Coprocessor for QR-UOV Signature
summary: QR-UOV is a Quotient Ring Unbalanced Oil and Vinegar (UOV) multivariate quadratic (MQ) signature scheme that has progressed to round-3 of the post-quantum cryptography (PQC) additional signatures call by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Until now, for architectural efficiency and performance trade-offs, QR-UOV has been evaluated only on software platforms and has never been considered on hardware, such as field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). To address this, we are the first to provide a complete QR-UOV hardware implementation through a flexible and unified QUISA coprocessor design, which supports instruction-driven execution for key generation, signing, and verification across all three NIST security levels (SL-I, SL-III, SL-V). The proposed architecture features extensive throughput optimizations by parallelizing key QR-UOV module operations, such as the pseudorandom byte generator, hashing, and rejection sampling. To minimize hardware resources, we propose a modular arithmetic unit with finite-field reduction based on the shift-add folding method. The design introduces a linear system solver for QUISA based on LU decomposition with partial pivoting and a sample solution module, operating over the prime field Fq (q = 127). We comprehensively evaluate QUISA on an Artix-7 FPGA at 80 MHz up to the post-place-and-route stage, utilizing 11,144 slices and 35,248 look-up tables. For higher SL-V security levels, it completes key generation, signing, and verification in 30.4M, 3.8M, and 2.8M clock cycles, respectively.

title: TabK: Amortized Bayesian Estimation of the Number of Clusters in Tabular Data
summary: Estimating the number of clusters, $k$, is a fundamental prerequisite for most clustering algorithms. Traditionally, this estimation has relied on computationally expensive grid searches over internal cluster validity indices (CVIs) or adaptive clustering algorithms, both constrained by specific statistical assumptions. We introduce TabK, a zero-shot, permutation-invariant transformer architecture that frames the estimation of $k$ as an amortized Bayesian inference problem for tabular data. TabK leverages a novel Quantile Feature Encoder (QFE) to extract position-free, content-derived representations from empirical marginal distributions. By learning a generalized structural bias over a diverse synthetic prior, TabK estimates the number of clusters in a single forward pass per ensemble member. Evaluated across 50 diverse real-world benchmarks, TabK outperforms all competing methods, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) value of 1.04 compared to 2.14 for the closest competitor. TabK also achieves the lowest average inference time, producing estimates in less than one second on average and running $2\times$ faster than TabClustPFN and $30\times$ faster than traditional CVIs such as Silhouette and Calinski-Harabasz. Code is available at https://github.com/mrbakhtyari/TabK.

title: G-Wave: Bit-to-Waveform Generation for Adaptive Wireless Communications
summary: Wireless waveforms are traditionally hand-designed for general propagation conditions, rather than adapted to each specific environment. Existing neural transceivers seek such adaptation, but often rely on relatively simple architectures with limited long-range modeling capability. More expressive Transformer-based generative architectures are difficult to apply directly because wireless communication demands extremely accurate bit recovery, often with BER below 0.1%, while providing no ground-truth waveform supervision. To address these limitations, we introduce G-Wave, a channel-conditioned generative transceiver that directly synthesizes environment-adaptive physical time-domain waveforms from bits. G-Wave consists of Transformer-based transmitter and receiver models equipped with a multiscale architecture that combines long-range sequence modeling with fine-grained signal synthesis to meet the stringent precision required for communication. The two models are jointly optimized end-to-end using only bit-reconstruction error, allowing the waveform itself to be discovered without waveform labels. Across diverse 3GPP wireless environments, G-Wave achieves lower BER than the SOTA neural transceiver (DeepOFDM) and a strong conventional baseline (OFDM) under estimated channel information, reducing mean BER by 42.4% and 72.6%, respectively.

title: RF-Florence: Unified RF Detection and Physical Grounding with a Foundation Model
summary: Reliable signal detection is essential for spectrum sharing and intelligent sensing in sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks. Wideband radio-frequency (RF) monitoring must locate emissions and identify those satisfying waveform-family and physical constraints. The latter task, physical grounding, requires query meaning to agree with measurable signal attributes. RF-Florence unifies three tasks---full-scene detection, physical grounding, and supplied-region recognition---through a shared pretrained foundation model. Calibrated spectrograms connect localization coordinates to time and frequency, while common event targets and explicit predicates align task outputs with requests. On synthetic mixtures with family--attribute combinations withheld from training, structured queries improve mean grounding F1 by 7.66 percentage points over natural language. Under the tested two-path channel, direct grounding with structured queries exceeds a You Only Look Once (YOLO) detector followed by rule-based filtering by 3.44 points in mean F1. These results show the value of aligning query expressions with the signal families and physical variables that define the requested event set.

title: Suppressing Chaos Without Silencing Excitable Oscillators
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos
summary: A negative Lyapunov exponent is not a sufficient goal for controlling an excitable oscillator. A gain can remove chaos by removing the excitation that the model is meant to keep. This manuscript studies that failure mode in three models: the forced FitzHugh--Nagumo neuron, the forced Aliev--Panfilov cardiac cell, and the autonomous Hindmarsh--Rose neuron. Chaos is measured by the largest state Lyapunov exponent. Excitation is measured by threshold crossings, by the excursion of the fast variable, and by the firing rate. Recovery damping, tracking of an unstable periodic orbit, Pyragas delayed feedback, and a change of the fast time scale are compared on the same chaotic regimes. In the forced models, large damping and large rate changes reach regularity by silencing the cell, while tracking and delayed feedback keep firing. In the autonomous model, recovery damping raises the firing rate several-fold instead. A classical matrix-measure bound links these outcomes to the channel through which the gain acts. A constant-metric contraction certificate coexists with substantial firing only under tracking, which subtracts a gain from the fast direction.

title: Who Is Prompt-Injecting Coding Agents? An Empirical Study of Hidden AI-Directed Text on GitHub
comment: 20 pages, 6 figures, 17 tables. Data and detection tool: https://github.com/rdwr-gabin/github-ipi-in-the-wild
summary:
AI coding agents now triage issues, review pull requests and pick up tasks inside GitHub repositories, and to do so they read text that anyone with a GitHub account can write. This makes GitHub a prime surface for indirect prompt injection, in which instructions embedded in untrusted content steer a model that later processes it. Prior work has demonstrated such attacks against agents on GitHub in controlled settings, but how often they occur in practice, who deploys them, and for what purpose remain unknown.
  We present the first large-scale empirical study of AI-directed hidden text on GitHub. We analyzed roughly 145 million issues, pull requests, comments and README files, detected text that GitHub does not render to a human reader but that an agent receives in full, and filtered it with a two-stage LLM classification, a template provenance check and an exhaustive manual review. We identify 2,281 validated findings in issues, pull requests and comments (16 per million items), and AI-directed hidden text in the READMEs of 107 repositories.
  We find a heterogeneous ecosystem of four uses: attacks on other parties' agents, defensive text that restricts agents, content override that steers what they write, and first-party orchestration, in which projects coordinate their own agents through hidden markers. Attacks are rare (about one in 3.3 million items) but aimed at maintainers' own triage, review and CI agents. Orchestration accounts for two thirds of the findings in issues, pull requests and comments, grew fivefold in four months, and forms a control channel that anyone who can comment can imitate. Replayed offline against five models we tested, the attacks succeed against one small, fast model in 19% of cases, and against none once HTML comments are stripped. We release our detection tool and every finding.

title: Which Loans, Not How Many: Exactly Level-Invariant, Anytime-Valid Monitoring of Deployed Risk Models
summary: A refinancing wave can change the number of mortgage prepayments without changing the relationship between scores and prepayment. In a logistic model, conditioning on the monthly count removes the intercept from the likelihood of which loans prepay. Our fixed-start slope product tests a lower bound on the calibration slope. At threshold 20 its probability of ever crossing under the null is at most 5%. The restarted level sum tracks departures from intercept tolerance. A confidence sequence estimates a constant slope, and the restart-intersection rule detects changes in that slope. A continuous mixture avoids the off-grid width floor of a discrete prior. On Freddie Mac loans, fixed-slope resampling reproduces 78% of maintained-model monthly AUC variance in development and 70% in the holdout (95% intervals 57-100% and 48-100%). From fresh holdout starts, the restarted level sum crosses on both paths, and the fixed-start slope product stays below threshold on both. The restart-intersection rule signals a downward change for the frozen model in April 2018 and an upward change for the maintained model in a supplementary run in August 2019.

title: Several families of linear codes via weight functions of three-weight codes
summary: Recently, Huang et al. proposed a general framework for deriving new linear codes from a given code by applying weight functions to the set of codewords with a prescribed Hamming weight in [A structural theory of linear codes from weight functions: constructions, geometry and applications, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, DOI:10.1109/TIT.2026.3742840, 2026]. While this method was systematically developed for two-weight codes and yielded several families of projective two-weight codes, extending it to codes with more weights remains an interesting and challenging problem. In this paper, we generalize this construction to three-weight codes by employing a well-known family of ternary three-weight cyclic codes. By determining the weight distribution of every codimension-one subcode, as well as the distribution of fixed-weight codewords across these subcodes, we completely characterize the behavior of the weight-function construction on this family. As a result, we obtain three classes of linear codes with four nonzero weights and explicitly determine their parameters. Furthermore, the results show that these obtained codes are self-orthogonal and minimal.

title: Approximate Convex Decomposition (ACD) with Divide and Conquer Strategy for DRL-Based BS Localization
summary: Optimal base station (BS) placement is a fundamental challenge in wireless localization. Conventional optimization approaches may become computationally demanding as the geometric complexity of the environment increases, limiting their scalability to realistic building layouts. This paper proposes an Approximate Convex Decomposition (ACD)-based divide-and-conquer framework integrated with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for optimizing BS placement. The proposed approach exploits the geometric structure of building layouts by partitioning the original environment into smaller sub-regions using cuts associated with reflex vertices. Furthermore, the proposed solution is bench-marked against DRL without ACD and with the optimal solution obtained by exhaustive search. Results show the superiority of the proposed approach and that it approaches the optimal solution.

title: Deliverable Frequency Regulation Reserve for VPPs via Transmission-Distribution Co-Simulation
comment: Submitted to the 2027 IEEE Power & Energy Society General Meeting (PESGM)
summary: Aggregations of distributed energy resources can provide frequency regulation services. However, device-level power headroom may not accurately represent the power deliverable at the transmission-distribution interface. This paper proposes a bidirectional, storage-aware power-sharing framework for a virtual power plant (VPP). Delivery factors obtained from the perturbations used to construct the voltage-sensitivity matrix account for feeder losses and voltage-dependent loads, while battery energy limits and state-of-charge weights are included in the allocation. The framework is evaluated using the IEEE 8500-node feeder and IEEE 14-bus system. The proposed method tracks the feeder-head request within 2% compared with 23-26% over-delivery under the injection-headroom framework. It also sustains the requested power response 22% longer before reaching the storage energy limit. Moreover, communicating the updated VPP reserve to the transmission system operator reduces the post-transient integrated area control error by 80% relative to fixed reserve registration.

title: Reporting Differential Privacy Guarantees via Operationally Equivalent $\varepsilon$: What Does $\varepsilon=19.61$ Mean for the 2020 U.S. Census?
comment: 33 pages, 4 figures, 9 tables. Revised and extended version of a preliminary Japanese paper presented at the Computer Security Symposium 2026 (CSS 2026). Reproduction code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23695034
summary: The large value $\varepsilon=19.61$, reported as an approximate differential privacy (ADP) parameter for the 2020 U.S. Census, has prompted doubts about the adequacy of Census privacy protection. It was obtained by converting component zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP) guarantees to ADP at $δ=10^{-10}$. A single ADP pair can substantially loosen the original upper bound on the power (true positive rate) of a distinguishing test. At significance level $α$, we express the original bound as the smallest pure differential privacy (DP) parameter giving the same power bound. We call this the $α$-operationally equivalent $\varepsilon$. The full curve represents the original bound exactly on $(0,1)$, even when the bound is nonconcave. For maximum-power curves and bounds derived from trade-off functions, we characterize the extrema of operationally equivalent $\varepsilon$ over an interval of significance levels. When finite, they give the parameters of the pure DP bounds that enclose the original power bound on that interval. The mapping preserves the ordering of power bounds at each significance level. For Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms with equal noise variance, conversion to single ADP pairs or Gaussian DP envelopes can reverse this ordering. For the P.L. 94-171 redistricting data, we reproduce the reported $\varepsilon=19.61$ as the sum of rounded component ADP values. The published zCDP guarantee yields operationally equivalent $\varepsilon$ values of approximately 4.25, 2.94, and 3.18 at significance levels of 1%, 5%, and 10%, respectively. Converting the same guarantee to a single ADP pair at $δ=10^{-10}$ gives power bounds near 1 at all three levels. The pure DP scale thus clarifies constraints on distinguishing attacks that are difficult to discern from the reported $\varepsilon=19.61$.

title: Toward Adversarially Robust World Models
summary: Latent dynamic world models have proven to be highly versatile tools for embodied artificial intelligence systems, enabling online action planning, safe policy evaluation, and scalable policy learning. However, this versatility makes world models a vulnerable and centralized point of failure as a compromised model can impact planning, evaluation, and training at once. Therefore it is critical that the security and robustness properties of world models are properly understood before they are universally deployed in embodied AI systems. In this work we take a unifying approach towards this understanding, developing two novel attacks against world models, named state hallucination and dynamic shift attacks, aimed directly at impacting downstream systems, and proposing a new theoretical lens through which to study the robustness of latent dynamic world models. Through our analysis we identify robust latent space encoders as the key component of robust world models. We empirically validate this finding on four separate latent dynamic world model families, studying Dino World Model, Le World Model, r2Dreamer, and Cosmos 3, demonstrating significant improvements in robustness through adversarial encoder model training.

title: Evidence Toward a Conjecture in List Recoverability of Folded Reed--Solomon Codes
summary: This paper investigates the list-recoverability of folded Reed--Solomon codes and provides new evidence toward a recent conjecture. Chen--Zhang (STOC 2025) established that for any $\ell,a \ge 2$ and $L = \ell^a - 1$, if a folded Reed--Solomon code of rate $R$ is $(ρ,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, then $ρ\leq \frac{L+1-\ell}{L+1}(1-\frac{aR}{a-1}).$ It is conjectured that this upper bound is tight. We provide two pieces of evidence concerning this conjecture. First, we prove that explicit folded Reed--Solomon codes of rate arbitrarily close to $\tfrac{a-1}{a+\ell-2}$ are $(0,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, which confirms the conjecture in the special case $ρ=0$ and $\ell=2$. Second, we show that for any $R\in(0,\tfrac{a-1}{a})$, there are rates arbitrarily close to $R$ at which attaining the conjectured bound requires exponentially large alphabets. This mirrors the phenomenon observed by Alrabiah--Guruswami--Li (SODA 2024), where achieving the generalized Singleton bound in the list-decoding setting also necessitates exponential alphabet size.

title: DIBEM: Diffusion-Based Error Mitigation for Uncertainty-Aware UWB Localization
summary: Ultra-wideband (UWB) localization degrades substantially under Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) propagation, where multipath and obstruction induce complex ranging error distributions that are poorly represented by fixed parametric models. We propose Diffusion-based Error Mitigation (DIBEM), an uncertainty-aware framework that learns the conditional ranging error distribution directly from six compact Channel Impulse Response (CIR) statistics. Rather than predicting a deterministic correction or restricting uncertainty to a Gaussian or fixed mixture family, DIBEM uses a conditional diffusion model with denoising diffusion implicit model sampling to generate link-specific error samples. The resulting empirical distributions are incorporated into maximum likelihood position estimation. This allows localization to account for heterogeneous ranging uncertainty across anchor-tag links. Experiments across four indoor environments show that DIBEM achieves the lowest negative log-likelihood for NLoS ranging errors and the lowest or tied-lowest mean localization error across all environments. Compared with least squares approaches, DIBEM reduces mean localization error by up to 64.8 percent, while improving over Gaussian and mixture density probabilistic models by up to 15.8 percent and 14.0 percent, respectively. Results demonstrate the potential of diffusion-based conditional error modeling for uncertainty-aware UWB localization, particularly under challenging NLoS propagation.

title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation
summary: Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages.
